description:
About the Position

Radboudumc recruits a promotendus (doctoral candidate) for the DACIL project, an evaluation of a digital COPD coach, based in Nijmegen. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) places a heavy burden on patients and healthcare systems, and digital coaching promises personalised support for self-management between clinic visits. The doctoral project evaluates the validity and diagnostic value of the digital coach's AI-based measurements and sensor data within a randomised controlled trial, asking whether the technology improves care without adding burden or inequality.

The position is a salaried four-year doctoral appointment under the Dutch CAO-NU collective agreement at Radboudumc. The doctoral candidate will contribute to the RCT protocol and execution, analyse sensor and app data, assess diagnostic accuracy against clinical references, and study how patients and professionals experience the technology. Because the research runs within Dutch clinical settings and with Dutch-speaking patients, professional working proficiency in Dutch is expected.

Candidate Profile and Working Environment

Applicants hold a master's degree in health sciences, medicine, biomedical sciences or a related field, with an interest in digital health, AI validation and clinical evaluation methods. Experience with RCT procedures, sensor data or implementation research is an advantage. Radboudumc provides structured doctoral training, and the candidate joins a digital-health research team spanning pulmonology, data science and health technology assessment.

Highlights

  • PhD on a digital COPD coach within the DACIL project
  • Randomised controlled trial evaluation
  • Validity and diagnostic value of AI and sensor data
  • Salaried employment under the CAO-NU agreement
  • Digital-health research across pulmonology and data science
  • Radboudumc academic medical centre environment

About Radboudumc

Radboudumc is the academic medical centre of Nijmegen, connected to Radboud University. It combines specialised patient care, research and education with a focus on prevention and personalised medicine, and hosts one of the Netherlands' leading clinical research environments. Doctoral researchers work in multidisciplinary teams spanning clinical departments, the Radboud Institute for Health Sciences and technology partners.
